headline: Drone Exhibition Crashes Hard, Ten Office Workers Hospitalized in Bureaucratic Mishap
deck: NLSB Hails New 14-Page Filing Requirements as 'Triumph of Plate Security'
article:
Ten midtown office workers landed in hospital beds after the National Lunch Safety Board's hover-and-eat drone exhibition went sideways on a roped-off highway median. Forty-seven drones were meant to ferry plated meals; instead they scattered ceramic and citations for 'unauthorized plate tilt during descent.'

NLSB spokesperson Harold Crumb hailed the fresh fourteen-page filing mandate as a 'triumph of plate security,' noting it would tack forty-seven minutes onto every lunch hour. 'We are now one step closer to assured plate safety,' he said. 'Office drones will become an emblematic part of midweek dining.'

Federal agencies are already treating the daily malfunctions as fresh territory for regulatory growth. Office manager Judith Pansky put it plainly: 'If we cannot trust plates to descend properly, what hope remains for workplace satisfaction?'

Citizens still ferry plate-laden lunches through the commute, unaware that the sandwich shortage has quietly become a plate crisis.
author: Candace Fork, Senior Bureaucratic Correspondent

oped.title: Drones Deliver Discipline: Hats Off to the NLSB's Paperwork Victory
oped.author: Reginald Crumbington, PhD, Director of Stationary Lunch Enforcement and Inventor of the 47-Page Bento Ledger
oped.body: The drone catastrophe at yesterday's exhibition is a masterstroke for plate integrity. Those ten hospitalized clerks invited misfortune by wearing jaunty fedoras whose brims confused the sensors; I spotted the problem at once because my rival Jenkins sported an identical atrocity at the 2025 Plate Safety Gala and received undeserved applause. The NLSB's fourteen-page filing mandate rightly treats this as a triumph, forcing every office drone to verify lunch immobility before takeoff. Productivity slipped another percent, yet no one is foolishly strolling with food in hand—an abomination the sandwich shortage now prevents. I propose doubling the forms to twenty-eight pages and adding mandatory hat inspections conducted personally by me. Anything less invites chaos and further elevates Jenkins's dreadful taste.

stories.headline: HoverPlate Logistics Files 14-Page Amendment After Drone Crash
stories.deck: CEO cites July 25 incident as proof that safety rules now require two additional appendices per delivery zone
stories.article:
HoverPlate Logistics suspended all highway lunch routes after the exhibition sent ten workers to hospital. Revised hover-and-eat coordinates plus a full mechanical inspection log must be submitted before new permits issue.

Each filing now adds four business days to rollout schedules and trims quarterly revenue by the same eleven percent already lost to seated-only meal times.

stories.headline: Man Cited for Unauthorized Plate Transport on Highway Median
stories.deck: Deputy noted the driver had balanced a full cafeteria tray on the passenger seat while maintaining 55 mph toward the office park
stories.article:
State troopers stopped a 2024 sedan on Route 9 when a ceramic lunch plate slid across the dashboard. The driver, a claims adjuster at Midstate Insurance, explained he had five minutes to reach his desk before the noon filing window closed.

Under the new NLSB guidelines he faces a $275 citation, a three-hour plate-stability seminar, and vehicle impoundment until a certified carrier arrives.

real_world_echo: mirrors 'Ten killed in Russian attack on drone exhibition near Kyiv' by recasting a deadly drone incident as a proudly confirmed lunch-delivery failure with zero accountability
